headline: A Simple Touch Revives Dying Corals in Record Time
meta_description: Scientists discovered severely bleached corals can fully recover in 7 weeks simply by touching healthy genetic clones, offering hope for threatened reefs.
summary_short: Researchers found that dying corals regain full health in just 7 weeks when placed in contact with healthy, genetically identical corals—a breakthrough for reef restorat…
body:
In a discovery that could transform coral reef conservation, scientists at Stanford's Doerr School of Sustainability have shown that severely bleached corals can make a complete recovery in just seven weeks by touching healthy, genetically identical clones. In laboratory experiments, corals that had turned white and were dying regained their vibrant colors and full health simply through physical contact with a healthy fragment from the same coral animal. The research, published in Science Advances on October 14, represents the fastest documented recovery from coral bleaching and opens a new path for saving reefs threatened by climate-driven ocean heat waves.

The breakthrough emerged from an unexpected observation in 2025, when researcher Steve Palumbi noticed two coral fragments—one healthy, one bleached—had fallen against each other in an aquarium. Where they touched, the bleached coral began returning to color. Collins designed a controlled experiment using ten pairs of coral fragments: five pairs touching, five separated by only millimeters. The results were stark: every bleached fragment that made contact recovered completely, while separated fragments died.

The mechanism behind this rapid healing is surprisingly elegant. Genetically identical corals recognize and fuse their tissues when they touch, creating tiny channels that allow beneficial algae and nutrients to transfer between fragments. Within three days, algae began moving into the damaged coral. Remarkably, just five days of contact was sometimes enough to trigger complete recovery—the algae then reproduced at extraordinary speed inside their new host, doubling roughly every four days. This finding suggests that once beneficial algae take hold in a bleached coral, they flourish independently, restoring the energy supply the coral desperately needs. As climate change intensifies, this simple, elegant solution offers genuine hope for reef restoration efforts worldwide.
quick_facts: Stanford researchers discovered bleached corals fully recover in 7 weeks through touch
Study published October 14, 2026 in Science Advances journal
Just 5 days of contact with healthy clones sometimes triggered complete healing
Beneficial algae doubled every 4 days inside recovered coral fragments
Finding based on laboratory experiments with genetically identical coral pairs
